nl.statement: Finite-alphabet i.i.d. observational world, in TWO explicitly bridged views. (a) CANONICAL / statement view: one observed unit is O = (X, A, Y) : Fin d x Bool x Bool; the single-observation law P is a probability Measure (built from a PMF) on that finite type with ARBITRARY cell masses; the n-sample law is the finite i.i.d. product Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => P), and every statement, estimator (a measurable Fin n -> Obs -> R) and the minimax inf/sup live HERE. (b) AMBIENT view, used only to import IIDSample-typed Causalean declarations: the infinite i.i.d. product Omega_inf = (ℕ -> Obs) with mu_inf = MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => P), whose coordinate process Z i omega = omega i is a genuine Causalean.Stat.IIDSample (ℕ -> Obs) Obs mu_inf P. BRIDGE (both directions available, in scope, for arbitrary P): Causalean.Stat.iidSample_finN_pushforward pushes mu_inf forward along the first-n-coordinates map onto Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => P), so any event/integral of the first n coordinates has equal mass in the two views. Primitives p_k = P(X=k), pi_k = P(A=1|X=k), mu_{ak} = E[Y|A=a,X=k], q_{aky} = P(X=k,A=a,Y=y) and the four-cell vector q_k are DERIVED real-valued readouts of the single-observation law P (finite sums over atoms), not independent fields. Scalars epsilon in (0,1/2], c in (0,inf) are plain reals. — HIGHEST-LEVERAGE REUSE DECISION, and the closest analogue in the library. Causalean.Estimation.MinimaxATE.Model realizes ALMOST exactly this world: Obs C = C x Bool x Bool over a Fintype C, binary treatment and binary outcome, obsReal/obsPMF/obsLaw the single-observation law, productLaw = Measure.pi over Fin n, nMSE the n-sample MSE, minimaxMiss the sup-over-class miss, plus the Chebyshev/Markov bridge nMiss_sq_le_nMSE. BLOCKING MISMATCH (verified by reading Causalean/Estimation/MinimaxATE/Model.lean lines 87-89 and 137-138): obsReal HARDCODES a UNIFORM covariate marginal (Fintype.card C)^{-1}, and `ate g` averages with the same uniform weights. This note's entire d^2/(n^2 log^2 n) rate is driven by ARBITRARY, in particular rare, cell masses p_k, so the uniform-P_X model is a strictly different (and for this result degenerate) world -> NOT a verbatim reuse; define-local a p_k-parameterized law in Basic.lean, keeping the Obs/productLaw/nMSE naming and construction pattern one-to-one so F3 can port MinimaxATE proof idioms. *** IIDSample BRIDGE (round-2 correction FLAG-IIDSample-world; see decisions.iid_world_is_finite_product_with_infinite_ambient_view). *** Causalean.Stat.IIDSample is the sampling primitive the concentration engines are typed over (Concentration.hoeffding_ge : (S : IIDSample Omega X mu P) -> ... -> mu.real {omega | eps <= S.sampleMean f n omega - integral f} <= exp(...), verified at Stat/Concentration/TailBounds/Hoeffding.lean:87-91), but it is a structure over an AMBIENT mu carrying an ℕ-INDEXED process Z : ℕ -> Omega -> X with iIndepFun Z mu (Stat/Sample.lean:42-48). The finite coordinate process of Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => P) is Fin n-indexed and therefore CANNOT itself be an IIDSample -- the prior plan's claim that this world 'exposes an IIDSample view of the product law' was wrong, and PiTransport does not repair it (iidSample_finN_pushforward CONSUMES an IIDSample to produce the finite product, it does not produce one). The world therefore carries view (b) EXPLICITLY: Basic.lean defines `iidOfInfinitePi (P) : IIDSample (ℕ -> Obs) Obs (Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => P)) P` with Z := fun i omega => omega i, meas := measurable_pi_apply, indep := ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun_infinitePi (fun _ => measurable_id), identDist/law := MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi_map_eval -- COMPILED 0-sorry against this repo's pinned Mathlib, so this is a verified ~10-line def, not a conjecture -- together with the transport corollary `finProductLaw_eq_map` : (Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => P)).map (fun omega (k : Fin n) => omega k) = Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => P), which is Causalean.Stat.iidSample_finN_pushforward APPLIED to iidOfInfinitePi (its Z k omega = omega k reduces definitionally). F3's usage pattern for every IIDSample-typed engine: state the target event as a measurable set E in Set (Fin n -> Obs), apply the engine on Omega_inf, then move the bound across with Causalean.Stat.event_pullback_along_iidSample / Measure.map_apply. This holds for ARBITRARY P (infinitePi needs only IsProbabilityMeasure P, which the PMF construction supplies), so it adds NO hypothesis to any statement and imposes no restriction on the cell masses -- exactly the point of keeping the finite product as the canonical statement world. Potential-outcome overlay on S1: binary potential outcomes Y(0), Y(1) : Omega -> Bool on the same finite probability space as (X, A, Y), with consistency (Y = Y(A) a.s.) and conditional exchangeability ((Y(0),Y(1)) indep A | X). Used only by the witness cluster; the estimation/minimax cluster is stated on the observed-data law alone. — Causalean.PO (POSystem, PO.Assumptions.Consistency, PO.Assumptions.IndepCF) is the framework analogue but is regime/graph-indexed over general measurable outcome spaces -- far heavier than the two-point binary overlay needed here, where def:two-category-witness supplies its OWN explicit full-data coupling ((Y(0),Y(1)) = (0, 1{X=1}), then A | X=k ~ Bernoulli(pi_k)) and prop:two-category-confounding VERIFIES consistency/exchangeability on it directly. Define-local over Mathlib with naming aligned to Causalean.PO. Search trace: read ../doc/API.md '## 8h. PO/' index (PO/Core/Regime, PO/Core/System, PO/Assumptions/Consistency, PO/Assumptions/IndepCF, PO/ID/Exact/ATE); no finite-alphabet binary PO overlay to reuse verbatim -> not found.

Functional / experiment-class / risk layer over S1: the overlap-restricted four-cell cone C_eps as a Set of four-vectors, the homogeneous cell contribution phi, the ATE functional tau(P) = sum_k phi(q_k), the experiment class E_{n,d,eps} of overlap-satisfying product laws, and the minimax risk R_{n,d,eps} = inf over measurable estimators of the sup-over-class MSE. — The risk shape (inf over measurable estimators of sup over a class of the n-sample MSE) is exactly Causalean.Estimation.MinimaxATE.Model's minimaxMiss/nMSE pattern, but over the p_k-parameterized class of S1 rather than the uniform-P_X structure-agnostic class, and in MSE (not miss-probability) form -> define-local, importing nMiss_sq_le_nMSE's Markov-bridge idiom. Estimator layer over S1: the balanced deterministic split I_0 = {1..floor(n/2)}, I_1 = the rest; split cell counts N^{(j)}_{aky}; four-cell exponent multi-indices r in N_0^4 with |r| = sum r_{ay}; the falling factorial z_r; the pilot-certified heavy/light partition (Hhat_n, Lhat_n); the light-cell factorial-moment polynomial contribution That_L; and the truncated hybrid tauhat_n^hyb. — z_r is Mathlib's Nat.descFactorial (z_r = z.descFactorial r, with z_0 = 1 definitional) -- REUSED, not redefined; Causalean.Stat.injectiveTupleCount_eq_descFactorial (Stat/UStatistic/OrderM/Basic.lean) is the exact combinatorial bridge 'ordered injective tuple count = falling factorial' that the note's eq (9) unbiasedness E[U_{k,r}] = q_k^r rests on, and is reused as the counting engine in Helpers/FactorialMoments.lean. Causalean.Stat.SampleSplit / OneShotSplit is the analogue for the two-fold split but is a RANDOM cross-fitting split over a growing index family; the note fixes a DETERMINISTIC balanced split I_0/I_1 of Fin n, so the split itself is a two-line Finset definition -> build-inline. The observed data are \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), where the covariate \(X\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), the treatment \(A\) and outcome \(Y\) are binary. For each category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) write \(p_k=P(X=k)\) for the category mass, \(\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)\) for the treatment probability, and, for each treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\) for the conditional mean outcome.

review.note: After unfolding IidSampling and Overlap, this is exactly the class of n-fold product laws from a probability law on Fin d × Bool × Bool satisfying 0 < epsilon ≤ 1/2 and the stated positive-cell overlap condition.
Unfolding vectorMass and vectorArmMass gives exactly nonnegative u₀₀,u₀₁,u₁₀,u₁₁ with εΣu ≤ u₁₀+u₁₁ ≤ (1-ε)Σu.
Unfolding cellPhi gives 0 at the zero vector and otherwise Σu·(u₁₁/(u₁₀+u₁₁)-u₀₁/(u₀₀+u₀₁)), on precisely overlapCone ε.

nl.frozen_body:
For a probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), with arbitrary masses on this finite observation alphabet, define, for \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), the joint cell mass
\[
q_{aky}=P(A=a,X=k,Y=y),
\]
and set
\[
q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1}).
\]
The average treatment effect functional is
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

review.note: Unfolding cellVector and cellPhi yields exactly Σₖ φ(qₖ), mathematically equal on overlap laws to Σₖ pₖ(μ₁ₖ-μ₀ₖ).

nl.statement:
With the deterministic splits \(I_0,I_1\), split sizes \(m_j\), scale \(L=\log(en)\), and split cell counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\) of \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}: Set \(A=6\), and put \(\lambda_0=256\), \(b_0=4096\), \(D_A=8\log(9A/8)=8\log(27/4)\), and
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A},\frac1{256D_A}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), put \(M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\}\) and \(B(n)=b_0L/m_1\). Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\), \(\alpha_0L\ge2\), \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\), and \(4M(n)/m_1\le3B(n)/4\). For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), and set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n=\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},\qquad \widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c.
\]
Put \(N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky}\), \(N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky}\), and
\[
\widehat h_k=\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\left\{\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}-\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}\right\}.
\]
Define \(H_M(x)=\{1-T_M(1-2x)\}/(2M^2)\), \(E_M(x)=H_M(x)/x\), and \(G_M(x)=\{1-E_M(x)\}/x\), using polynomial continuation at zero, and
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)-\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Here \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\), \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\), \(t_1(u)=u_{11}\), and \(t_0(u)=u_{01}\). Expand \(P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r\), set
\[
\widehat P_k=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},\quad \widehat T_{\mathcal H}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,\quad \widehat T_{\mathcal L}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k,
\]
and define \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}\). For \(n<N_0\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\) and use the ratio branch on every category. The estimator uses no overlap constant and is computable in \(O(dM^4)\) arithmetic operations.
nl.frozen_body:
Using the deterministic splits \(I_0,I_1\), split sizes \(m_j\), logarithmic scale \(L=\log(en)\), and split counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\) from \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, set
\[
A_0=6,\qquad \lambda_0=256,\qquad b_0=4096,
\]
\[
D_{A_0}=8\log(9A_0/8)=8\log(27/4),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A_0},\frac1{256D_{A_0}}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), define
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},\qquad B(n)=b_0L/m_1.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,\qquad 4M(n)^2\le m_1,\qquad 4M(n)/m_1\le 3B(n)/4.
\]
For every \(n\), define the pilot-certified heavy and light category sets
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n
=
\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c\quad(n\ge N_0),
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\quad(n<N_0),
\]
so that for \(n<N_0\) every category is treated by the ratio branch below. For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\).
Put
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky},
\]
and define the heavy-category ratio contribution
\[
\widehat h_k
=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}
\left\{
\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}
-
\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}{x},
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}{x},
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are interpreted by polynomial continuation at zero. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},\qquad s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\]
\[
t_1(u)=u_{11},\qquad t_0(u)=u_{01},
\]
and define the light-cell polynomial
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)
-
\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
For each category \(k\), define
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}
c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}.
\]
The heavy and light sums are
\[
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}
=
\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
The same calibrated estimator is used for every overlap level.

For \(d=2\) and \(0\le \epsilon\le 1\), set
\[
p_1=p_2=\frac12,\qquad
\pi_1=\epsilon,\qquad
\pi_2=1-\epsilon,\qquad
\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0,\qquad
\mu_{11}=1,\qquad
\mu_{12}=0.
\]
Define the corresponding full-data extension by drawing
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,\mathbf 1\{X=1\})
\]
setting \(Y=Y(A)\), and then drawing \(A\mid X=k\sim\mathsf{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\).

nl.statement: There are constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\) and a computable calibration of \(def:hybrid-estimator-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_\epsilon n\log n\) and every \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), its light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) obeys \[ E_P\!\left[\left\{\widehat T_{\mathcal L}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)\right\}^2\right]\le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2 n}\right\}. \] The calibration uses a polynomial approximation of \(\phi\) on the overlap-restricted four-cell cone and factorial-moment monomials from \(I_1\).

nl.statement:
Let \(m_0\asymp n\), \(L=\log(en)\), \(\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^c\), \(B_-=tL/(2m_0)\), and \(B_+=2tL/m_0\). For every \(K>0\), sufficiently large numerical \(t\) gives, uniformly over \(d\le cnL\),
\[
P\left(\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}\text{ or }\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}\right)\le C_Kn^{-K}.
\]
The choice \(t=256\) is valid for \(K=4\).

review.note: Unfolding logScale, pilotHeavyAt, pilotBadEvent, and IidSampling yields L=log(en), the count threshold N_k^(0)>tL, the B_-/B_+ inclusion failure event, uniform polynomial decay for sufficiently large t, and the t=256,K=4 specialization.

nl.statement:
For the threshold \(\lambda_0=256\), every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) admits \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\), and \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\),
\[
E_P\left[\left\{\widehat T_{\mathcal H}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)\right\}^2\right]\le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}.
\]

review.note: Unfolding heavyContribution, targetHeavy, componentErrorMSE, minimaxRate, ExperimentClass, and the eventually active heavyCells definition gives the lambda_0=256 heavy-cell MSE bound with exactly the stated epsilon-dependent constants, cutoff, dimension range, and experiment class.

nl.statement:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). Let \(\mathcal D_0^{(n,d)}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome subclass of \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) consisting of laws \(P^{\otimes n}\) with arbitrary masses \(p_k\ge0\), \(\sum_{k=1}^d p_k=1\), propensities satisfying \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category, arbitrary treated response means \(\mu_{1k}\in[0,1]\), and \(\mu_{0k}=0\) for every \(k\). Define \(\psi_1(P)=\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\mu_{1k}\). There are constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for all \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le b_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal D_0^{(n,d)}(\epsilon)}E_P[(\widehat\psi-\psi_1(P))^2]\ge a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\},
\]
where the infimum is over measurable estimators based on the fixed sample of size \(n\).

review.note: This sanctioned cited assumption self-containedly quantifies positive constants and an eventual sample-size threshold and lower-bounds the measurable-estimator minimax MSE over the defined fixed-sample binary control-zero overlap class by the stated minimaxRate.

nl.statement:
For fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(d\le b_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\ge a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}.
\]

review.note: Unfolding minimaxRate gives exactly 1/n+d²/(n²log²n); the existential cutoff encodes sufficiently large n, positive d is the alphabet-size domain, and hZeng exposes the paper's established cited one-arm premise.

nl.statement:
Define the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}=\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\), and every \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\),
\[
E_P[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2]\le\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2.
\]

review.note: centeredEstimator unfolds to the displayed 2/n centered score, ExperimentClass exactly supplies positive epsilon, epsilon≤1/2, iid product sampling and overlap, and mse is the stated expected squared error.
The inequality is exactly R_{n,d,1/2}≥1/(100n); hn and hd merely enforce the intrinsic positive sample-size and nonempty-alphabet domains required by the paper's notation.
After unfolding minimaxRisk, the two inequalities exactly match the endpoint bracket; hn and hd only make explicit the intrinsic positive sample-size and positive alphabet-size domain.

nl.statement:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,N_\epsilon\) for which the upper bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior} holds. For \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\), choose the hybrid when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}\le\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2,
\]
and otherwise choose \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\). The selected estimator has worst-case risk at most
\[
K_\epsilon\left[\frac1n+\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}\right],\qquad K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}.
\]

review.note: Unfolding selectedEstimator and minimaxRate gives exactly the paper's deterministic selector and K_epsilon=max{C_epsilon,4} envelope; the additional minimaxRisk≤worstCaseMSE conjunct is automatic from the minimax infimum over measurable estimators.

nl.statement:
For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(a_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,C_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and uniformly over \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\), the balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid in \(def:hybrid-estimator-handle\) satisfies
\[
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}\le\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}.
\]
Consequently, the minimax MSE has parametric order \(n^{-1}\) whenever \(d=O(\sqrt n\log n)\), and, along sequences in the displayed range, it converges to zero if and only if \(d=o(n\log n)\).

review.note: Unfolding ExperimentClass, minimaxRate, minimaxRisk, worstCaseMSE, and hybridEstimator gives the same uniform three-sided rate, parametric-order consequence, and sequencewise consistency equivalence; 0<d is the intrinsic nonempty-alphabet domain, the P/mu_n binders are admissible realization guards, and hZeng is the paper's sanctioned cited lower-bound input. | All three conjuncts are logically equivalent to the note. Conjunct 1 is the exact three-sided display a_ε·rate ≤ minimaxRisk ≤ worstCaseMSE(hybrid) ≤ C_ε·rate with minimaxRate unfolding to 1/n+d²/(n²log²n), worstCaseMSE=sup_{P∈E}E[(τ̂−τ)²], minimaxRisk=inf-sup; the extra P/mu_n/ExperimentClass and 0<d are nonemptiness-witness/alphabet-domain bookkeeping, not content. Conjunct 2 (∀K>0 ∃C_K, a_ε/n ≤ R ≤ C_K/n under d≤K√n log n) faithfully encodes 'parametric order n⁻¹ whenever d=O(√n log n)'. Conjunct 3 (R→0 ↔ ds/(ns log ns)→0 along eventually-in-range sequences) encodes 'converges to 0 iff d=o(n log n)'. The added hZeng hypothesis is the cited one-arm lower gate (status:cited); the ATE lower bound is not directly assumed but derived via the Lean-proved oneArmMinimaxRisk_le_minimaxRisk restriction — sanctioned citation, not laundering.

nl.statement:
The following conclusions hold.

\(\mathrm{(i)}\) The single computable hybrid \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\), with \(A=6\), \(\lambda_0=256\), \(b_0=4096\), and numerical \(\alpha_0\), does not take \(\epsilon\) as input. For every fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}.
\]
Thus fixed-class overlap adaptation requires no selector.

\(\mathrm{(ii)}\) For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1/2\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}=\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}E_P[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2]\le\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2.
\]

\(\mathrm{(iii)}\) For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le\mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le\frac1n.
\]

\(\mathrm{(iv)}\) Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,N_\epsilon\) from the fixed-interior upper theorem. For \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le\rho_\epsilon n\log n\), choose the hybrid when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\}\le\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2,
\]
and otherwise choose \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\). This deterministic choice satisfies
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le K_\epsilon\left[\frac1n+\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}\right],\qquad K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(v)}\) These fixed-class and endpoint conclusions do not assert a matching lower envelope for triangular arrays \(\epsilon=\epsilon_n\).

review.note: After unfolding the estimator, computability, rate, selector, worst-case MSE, minimax risk, experiment class, product law, and ATE functional, the Lean conjunction is equivalent to clauses (i)–(iv): it fixes the numerical epsilon-free hybrid and O(dM^4) realization, states the same fixed-interior and centered bounds, endpoint bracket, and deterministic combined envelope; clause (v) is faithfully reflected by the pointwise-in-epsilon quantifiers and absence of any triangular-array lower claim.

nl.statement:
Let \(L=\log(en)\), \(\ell=\log n\), \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), and \(m_1=|I_1|\). If \(n\ge N_0\) and \(L\ge240\), then
\[
0<\ell\le L\le2\ell,\qquad 0<m_1,\qquad n\le2m_1,\qquad M\le L,\qquad B\le\frac{8192L}{n},\qquad (6^{2M})^2L^6\le n.
\]
In particular \(1/m_1\le2/n\).

review.note: Unfolding logScale, polynomialDegree, bandwidth, and splitSize gives exactly the listed conjunction of calibration consequences under calibrationCutoff<=n and 240<=logScale n; 1/m_1<=2/n restates n<=2*m_1.

nl.statement: Let \(P\) be a single-observation law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\) and let \(n\in\mathbb N\). Write \(P^{\otimes\infty}\) for the law of the ambient infinite iid sequence \((O_i)_{i\ge1}\) generated by \(P\). Then the image of \(P^{\otimes\infty}\) under the coordinate restriction \((O_i)_{i\ge1}\mapsto(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) is the \(n\)-fold product law \(P^{\otimes n}\) of \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}; that is, under \(P^{\otimes\infty}\) the initial segment \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) has law \(P^{\otimes n}\).

review.note: Lean's finProductLaw_eq_map states that the ambient infinite product Measure.infinitePi pushes forward under restriction to the first n coordinates to Measure.pi over Fin n; instantiated at obsLaw P this is exactly the identification of the law of \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) with \(P^{\otimes n}\) (productLaw).

nl.statement:
Fix \(n\ge N_0\) and a category \(k\), and abbreviate \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\) as in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}. Let \(g_{M,j}\) be the coefficients of the polynomial continuation \(G_M\), so that \(G_M(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}x^j\), and for an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), a cell index \(c\in\{0,1\}^2\), and integers \(0\le t\le j\), let \(r^{a,c,j,t}\) be the four-cell exponent vector determined by \(u^{r^{a,c,j,t}}=u_cu_{a1}u_{a0}^{\,t}u_{a1}^{\,j-t}\). With the split counts \(N^{(1)}_{bky}\) and split size \(m_1\) of \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, define the sparse arm contributions
\[
\widehat A_{a,k}=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}\sum_{t=0}^{j}\sum_{c\in\{0,1\}^2}B^{-1}g_{M,j}B^{-j}\binom jt\frac{\prod_{b,y}(N^{(1)}_{bky})_{r^{a,c,j,t}_{by}}}{(m_1)_{|r^{a,c,j,t}|}}.
\]
Then the factorial-moment polynomial estimate \(\widehat P_k\) of \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} admits the sparse two-arm representation \(\widehat P_k=\widehat A_{1,k}-\widehat A_{0,k}\).

review.note: Lean formalizes the factorial lift as factorialPolynomialContribution, which is written in the sparse arm/binomial form, so factorialPolynomialContribution_eq_sparseArms closes by rfl; the node makes that sparse two-arm representation of \(\widehat P_k\) citable rather than re-deriving it from the coefficient-support display of \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}.

nl.statement:
Let \(P\) be a single-observation law on \(d\) categories and let \(k\) be a category. For every \(n\ge N_0\), the factorial-moment polynomial estimate of the light-cell contribution has exact mean
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[\widehat P_k\right]=P_{M(n),B(n)}(q_k).
\]

review.note: The Lean statement integrates factorialPolynomialContribution over the iid product law and equates it with cellApproxPolynomial evaluated at the four-cell vector q_k; unfolding these gives E[P_k hat]=P_{M,B}(q_k) under the calibration cutoff.

nl.statement:
Write \(P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_r c_ru^r\) in multi-index form over the four cells. For every degree \(M\), scale \(B>0\), and nonnegative four-cell vector \(v\), the absolute-coefficient envelope obeys
\[
\sum_r|c_r|\,v^r\le B\,6^M\max\left\{\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^2,\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^M\right\};
\]
in particular it is at most \(B\,6^M\) whenever \(s(v)\le B\).

review.note: The Lean statement bounds the support sum of |coeff| times the monomial at v for cellApproxPolynomial M B by B*6^M*max((vectorMass v/B)^2,(vectorMass v/B)^M); the s(v)<=B specialization makes the max factor at most one.

nl.statement:
Let \(\bar P_k\) be the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\) (the exact mean of \(\widehat P_k\) under the stated conditions). If \(m_1>0\), \(M(n)\ge1\), \(B(n)>0\), \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\), and the shifted mass obeys \(p_k+4M(n)/m_1\le B(n)\) together with \(p_k\le B(n)\), then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2\right]\le8(\mathrm e+1)\left\{B(n)\,6^{M(n)}\right\}^2.
\]

review.note: The Lean statement centers factorialPolynomialContribution at sparsePolynomialMean and bounds the second moment under the product law by 8(e+1)(bandwidth*6^degree)^2, with hypotheses 0<splitSize, 0<degree, 0<bandwidth, 4M^2<=m_1, and the shifted-mass inequality; the sparse mean equals E[P_k hat] because M<=m_1 follows from 1<=M and 4M^2<=m_1.

nl.statement:
Let \(\bar P_k\) be the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\). For distinct categories \(k\ne l\) with \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\), if \(M(n)\ge1\), \(B(n)>0\), and \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\), then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)\left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)\right]\le\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)\,6^{M(n)}\right\}^2.
\]

review.note: The Lean statement bounds the centered cross moment of two factorialPolynomialContribution terms under the product law by 8*degree^2/splitSize*(bandwidth*6^degree)^2, with hypotheses k<>l, 0<degree, 0<bandwidth, 4M^2<=m_1, and unshifted mass at most bandwidth on both categories.

nl.statement:
Fix a degree \(M\ge1\), a scale \(B\), and \(\epsilon>0\). For every four-cell vector \(u\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\) with \(s(u)\le B\),
\[
\left|P_{M,B}(u)-\phi(u)\right|\le\frac{2B}{\epsilon M^2}.
\]

review.note: The Lean statement bounds |eval of cellApproxPolynomial M B at u minus cellPhi u| by 2B/(epsilon*M^2) for u in overlapCone epsilon with vectorMass u<=B; this is the Chebyshev reciprocal-approximation certificate in paper notation.

nl.statement:
Let \(P\) satisfy overlap at some level \(\epsilon\) and let \(S_k=\mathbf 1\{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n\}\). If \(n\ge N_0\) and \(\log(en)\ge240\), then the false-light target error obeys
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\sum_{k:p_k>B(n)/4}S_k\left(\widehat P_k-\phi(q_k)\right)\right\}^2\right]\le8(\mathrm e+1)8192^2\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\},
\]
with a constant not depending on \(\epsilon\), \(d\), or \(P\).
nl.frozen_body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} For every category \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), the treatment probability satisfies
\[
\epsilon \le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Calibration cutoff.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the least numerical cutoff satisfying the calibration inequalities used in the estimator.
\item \textbf{(Logarithmic scale.)} With \(L=\log(en)\), one has \(L\ge 240\).
\end{itemize}
For the pilot-light indicator \(S_k=\mathbf 1\{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n\}\), the selected false-light error over categories whose population mass exceeds the light-cell threshold satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[
\left\{
\sum_{\substack{k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\\ p_k>B(n)/4}}
S_k\bigl(\widehat P_k-\phi(q_k)\bigr)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)8192^2
\left\{
\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

review.note: The Lean statement integrates the square of selectedFalseLightError (the sum over falseLightSet, i.e. categories with p_k>bandwidth/4, of lightIndicator times the centered target error) and bounds it by 8(e+1)8192^2 times lightAsymptoticRate n d, under Overlap epsilon P, the calibration cutoff, and 240<=logScale n.

nl.statement:
Let \(P\) satisfy overlap at level \(\epsilon>0\), let \(H\) be a deterministic set of categories with \(p_k>0\) for every \(k\in H\), fix an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and draw an iid \(P\)-sample of size \(m\). With counts computed from this sample, the aggregate centered ratio residual
\[
\mathcal R_a(H)=\sum_{k\in H}N_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}>0\}}{N_{ak}}\left\{N_{ak1}-\mu_{ak}N_{ak}\right\}
\]
obeys
\[
E\left[\mathcal R_a(H)^2\right]\le\frac{2m}{\epsilon}\sum_{k\in H}p_k:
\]
all off-diagonal residual products cancel exactly, and the surviving diagonal loses only one factor \(1/\epsilon\) through overlap.

review.note: The Lean statement bounds the second moment of fixedRatioResidual (tupleRatioCoeff, equal to N_k/N_ak on {N_ak>0} and zero otherwise, times the summed armOutcomeResidual, equal to N_ak1-mu_ak*N_ak) over the m-fold product law by (2m/epsilon)*sum of cell masses, under Overlap epsilon P, 0<epsilon, and positive mass on H.

nl.statement:
Let \(P\) satisfy overlap at level \(\epsilon>0\), fix \(B>0\) and a deterministic set \(H\) of categories with \(p_k\ge B\) for every \(k\in H\), an arm \(a\), and an iid \(P\)-sample of size \(m\ge3\). With \(Z_{ak}=N_k\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}=0\}\) and \(u=((m-2)/2)\epsilon\), the missing-arm count obeys
\[
E\left[\left(\sum_{k\in H}Z_{ak}\right)^2\right]\le m+m^2\left[\frac{|H|}{\left\{((m-2)/2)\epsilon\right\}^2B}\right]^2.
\]
The diagonal contributes at most \(m\); the off-diagonal terms and the exponentially small part of the diagonal combine into the square of the mass-exponential sum \(\sum_{k\in H}p_ke^{-up_k}\), which the mass floor \(p_k\ge B\) converts into the displayed envelope.

review.note: The Lean statement bounds the second moment of fixedMissingCount (the sum over H of the category count on the event that arm a is unobserved in that category) over the m-fold product law by m+m^2*(|H|/((((m-2)/2)epsilon)^2 B))^2, under 3<=m, Overlap epsilon P, 0<epsilon, 0<B, and B<=p_k on H.

nl.statement:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), a probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), a category \(k\), and multi-indices \(r,s\) over the four treatment--outcome cells with \(|r|\le|s|\). For a multi-index \(r\), write \(\mathfrak m_{k,r}=\prod_{(a,y)}\bigl(N^{(1)}_{aky}\bigr)_{r_{ay}}/(m_1)_{|r|}\) for the normalized factorial-moment monomial of category \(k\) computed from the estimation split, where \((z)_t\) is the falling factorial. Assume \(m_1>0\) and \(4|s|^2\le m_1\). Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\bigl[\mathfrak m_{k,r}\,\mathfrak m_{k,s}\bigr]\le \mathrm e\,\prod_{(a,y)}\bigl(q_{aky}\bigr)^{r_{ay}}\prod_{(a,y)}\Bigl(q_{aky}+\tfrac{|s|}{m_1}\Bigr)^{s_{ay}}.
\]
nl.frozen_body:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and four-cell multi-indices \(r,s\). Using the split counts and split size in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, let
\[
\mathfrak m_{k,r}
=
\frac{\prod_{(a,y)}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\]
where \((z)_t\) denotes the falling factorial and \(|r|=\sum_{(a,y)}r_{ay}\). Let \(q_{aky}\) denote the treatment--outcome cell mass in category \(k\), as in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional}. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty estimation split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree ordering.)} \(|r|\le |s|\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size condition.)} \(4|s|^2\le m_1\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the iid product law generated by \(P\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\mathfrak m_{k,r}\mathfrak m_{k,s}\right]
\le \mathrm e\,\prod_{(a,y)}q_{aky}^{\,r_{ay}}
\prod_{(a,y)}
\left(q_{aky}+\frac{|s|}{m_1}\right)^{s_{ay}} .
\]

review.note: Lean bounds the product integral of two truncated factorial monomials (degrees ordered, 4|s|^2 <= split size) by e times the raw cell-mass monomial at r and the (|s|/m_1)-shifted cell-mass monomial at s. OPERATOR ADJUDICATION 2026-08-20: fixed renderer typo \le\ne -> \le \mathrm e (Euler constant, matching the Lean bound's exp 1 factor); body otherwise the audited render.

nl.statement:
Let \(M\ge1\) and \(z\ge0\). With \(g_{M,j}\) the coefficients of the polynomial continuation \(G_M\) of \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, the one-arm absolute coefficient sum \(g_M^+(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}|g_{M,j}|\,z^j\) satisfies
\[
g_M^+(z)\le 6^M\max\bigl\{1,;z^{M-2}\bigr\}.
\]

review.note: Lean's gpos M z is the absolute-coefficient sum of gPolynomial (the G_M continuation); gpos_bound gives gpos M z <= 6^M * max 1 (z^(M-2)) via the Chebyshev evaluation T_M(3) <= 6^M.

nl.statement:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the deterministic half-sample splits, their sizes, and the logarithmic scale
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},\qquad m_j=|I_j|,\qquad L=\log(en),
\]
and, for each split \(j\in\{0,1\}\), treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and outcome \(y\in\{0,1\}\), the split cell count
\[
N^{(j)}_{aky}=\#\{i\in I_j:(A_i,X_i,Y_i)=(a,k,y)\}.
\]
nl.frozen_body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the deterministic half-sample splits, their sizes, and the logarithmic scale
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},\qquad m_j=|I_j|,\qquad L=\log(en),
\]
and, for each split \(j\in\{0,1\}\), treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and outcome \(y\in\{0,1\}\), the split cell count
\[
N^{(j)}_{aky}=\#\{i\in I_j:(A_i,X_i,Y_i)=(a,k,y)\}.
\]

review.note: Bundles the deterministic split apparatus: splitIndices n j (first/second half-sample), splitSize (cardinality), and splitCellCount (per-split (a,k,y) cell count); L=log(en) is the logScale used throughout.
